method.description: Lexical/rendering divergence indicator; not a doctrinal truth score or majority vote.
method.normalization: case, punctuation, footnote markers, and common KJV archaisms normalized
method.public_ranking_guard: minimum 8 POB tokens and three length-compatible references

sources.bsb: Berean Standard Bible (Public Domain / CC0). bereanbible.com.
sources.asv: American Standard Version (1901; Public Domain). ebible.org/asv/.
sources.brenton: Brenton's translation of the Septuagint (1844/1851; Public Domain). ebible.org/eng-Brenton/.
sources.kjv: King James Version, ebible.org 2006 transcription (Public Domain in US).

pob.text: An oracle concerning Nineveh[a]. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.

spob.text: A prophetic message about Nineveh.[a] This book contains the vision of Nahum, a man from Elkosh.

public_domain_references.bsb: This is the burden against Nineveh, the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite:
public_domain_references.web: A revelation about Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
public_domain_references.asv: The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
public_domain_references.kjv: The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
public_domain_references.brenton: The burden of Nineve: the book of the vision of Naum the Elkesite.

pob.text: Yahweh is a jealous and avenging God[a]; Yahweh is avenging and full of wrath. Yahweh takes vengeance on his adversaries[c][b], and he keeps wrath for his enemies.

spob.text: Yahweh is a jealous God[a] who takes vengeance. Yahweh takes vengeance and is full of wrath. He takes vengeance on those who oppose him and stores up wrath for his enemies.

public_domain_references.bsb: The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; the LORD is avenging and full of wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on His foes and reserves wrath for His enemies.
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh is a jealous God and avenges. Yahweh avenges and is full of wrath. Yahweh takes vengeance on his adversaries, and he maintains wrath against his enemies.
public_domain_references.asv: Jehovah is a jealous God and avengeth; Jehovah avengeth and is full of wrath; Jehovah taketh vengeance on his adversaries, and he reserveth [wrath] for his enemies.
public_domain_references.kjv: God [is] jealous, and the LORD revengeth; the LORD revengeth, and [is] furious; the LORD will take vengeance on his adversaries, and he reserveth [wrath] for his enemies.
public_domain_references.brenton: God is jealous, and the Lord avenges; the Lord avenges with wrath; the Lord takes vengeance on his adversaries, and he cuts off his enemies.

pob.text: Yahweh is slow to anger and great in power[a], and he will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. Yahweh—his way is in the whirlwind and the storm, and clouds are the dust of his feet.

spob.text: Yahweh is slow to anger and great in power. He will never let the guilty go unpunished.[a] Yahweh’s way is in the whirlwind and the storm. Clouds are the dust beneath his feet.

public_domain_references.bsb: The LORD is slow to anger and great in power; the LORD will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His path is in the whirlwind and storm, and clouds are the dust beneath His feet.
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh is slow to anger, and great in power, and will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. Yahweh has his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
public_domain_references.asv: Jehovah is slow to anger, and great in power, and will by no means clear [the guilty]: Jehovah hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
public_domain_references.kjv: The LORD [is] slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit [the wicked:] the LORD hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds [are] the dust of his feet.
public_domain_references.brenton: The Lord is long-suffering, and his power is great, and the Lord will not hold any guiltless: his way is in destruction and in the whirlwind, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.

pob.text: He rebukes the sea and dries it up; he makes all the rivers run dry[a]. Bashan and Carmel wither; even the blossom of Lebanon withers.

spob.text: He rebukes the sea and dries it up. He makes every river run dry. The vegetation of Bashan and Carmel withers; even Lebanon’s blossoms wither.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: He rebukes the sea and dries it up; He makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the flower of Lebanon wilts.
public_domain_references.web: He rebukes the sea and makes it dry, and dries up all the rivers. Bashan and Carmel languish. The flower of Lebanon languishes.
public_domain_references.asv: He rebuketh the sea, and maketh it dry, and drieth up all the rivers: Bashan languisheth, and Carmel; and the flower of Lebanon languisheth.
public_domain_references.kjv: He rebuketh the sea, and maketh it dry, and drieth up all the rivers: Bashan languisheth, and Carmel, and the flower of Lebanon languisheth.
public_domain_references.brenton: He threatens the sea, and dries it up, and exhausts all the rivers: the land of Basan, and Carmel are brought low, and the flourishing [trees] of Libanus have come to nought.

pob.text: The mountains quake before him[a], and the hills melt away; the earth rises up before his face[b], the world and all who dwell in it.

spob.text: The mountains quake before him, and the hills melt away. The earth rises up in his presence—the world and everyone who lives in it.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The mountains quake before Him, and the hills melt away; the earth trembles at His presence— the world and all its dwellers.
public_domain_references.web: The mountains quake before him, and the hills melt away. The earth trembles at his presence, yes, the world, and all who dwell in it.
public_domain_references.asv: The mountains quake at him, and the hills melt; and the earth is upheaved at his presence, yea, the world, and all that dwell therein.
public_domain_references.kjv: The mountains quake at him, and the hills melt, and the earth is burned at his presence, yea, the world, and all that dwell therein.
public_domain_references.brenton: The mountains quake at him, and the hills are shaken, and the earth recoils at his presence, [even] the world, and all that dwell in it.

pob.text: Who can stand before his indignation? And who can rise up in the heat of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire[c][b][a], and the rocks are shattered by him.

spob.text: Who can stay on their feet before his indignation? Who can rise when his anger burns? His wrath pours out like fire, and the rocks shatter because of him.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Who can withstand His indignation? Who can endure His burning anger? His wrath is poured out like fire; even rocks are shattered before Him.
public_domain_references.web: Who can stand before his indignation? Who can endure the fierceness of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are broken apart by him.
public_domain_references.asv: Who can stand before his indignation? and who can abide in the fierceness of his anger? his wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are broken asunder by him.
public_domain_references.kjv: Who can stand before his indignation? and who can abide in the fierceness of his anger? his fury is poured out like fire, and the rocks are thrown down by him.
public_domain_references.brenton: Who shall stand before his anger? and who shall withstand in the anger of his wrath? his wrath brings to nought kingdoms, and the rocks are burst asunder by him.

pob.text: Yahweh is good[a], a stronghold in the day of distress[c][b]; he knows those who take refuge in him.

spob.text: Yahweh is good. He is a secure fortress when trouble comes. He knows those who seek shelter in him.

public_domain_references.bsb: The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of distress; He cares for those who trust in Him.
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knows those who take refuge in him.
public_domain_references.asv: Jehovah is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that take refuge in him.
public_domain_references.kjv: The LORD [is] good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.
public_domain_references.brenton: The Lord is good to them that wait on him in the day of affliction; and he knows them that reverence him.

pob.text: But with an overwhelming flood he will make a complete end of its place[a], and darkness will pursue his enemies.

spob.text: But with an overwhelming flood, he will completely destroy her place.[a] Darkness will pursue his enemies.

public_domain_references.bsb: But with an overwhelming flood He will make an end of Nineveh and pursue His enemies into darkness.
public_domain_references.web: But with an overflowing flood, he will make a full end of her place, and will pursue his enemies into darkness.
public_domain_references.asv: But with an over-running flood he will make a full end of her place, and will pursue his enemies into darkness.
public_domain_references.kjv: But with an overrunning flood he will make an utter end of the place thereof, and darkness shall pursue his enemies.
public_domain_references.brenton: But with an overrunning flood he will make an utter end: darkness shall pursue those that rise up against [him] and his enemies.

pob.text: What are you plotting against Yahweh? He will make a complete end[b][a]; trouble will not rise up a second time.

spob.text: What are you plotting against Yahweh? He will bring a complete end. Trouble will not rise again.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Whatever you plot against the LORD, He will bring to an end. Affliction will not rise up a second time.
public_domain_references.web: What do you plot against Yahweh? He will make a full end. Affliction won’t rise up the second time.
public_domain_references.asv: What do ye devise against Jehovah? he will make a full end; affliction shall not rise up the second time.
public_domain_references.kjv: What do ye imagine against the LORD? he will make an utter end: affliction shall not rise up the second time.
public_domain_references.brenton: What do ye devise against the Lord? he will make a complete end: he will not take vengeance by affliction twice at the same time.

pob.text: For though they are tangled like thorns[a], and drenched with their drink[b], they will be consumed like fully dry stubble.

spob.text: For even though[a] they are tangled together like thorns and soaked with drink,[b] they will be burned up like completely dry stalks left after harvest.

public_domain_references.bsb: For they will be entangled as with thorns and consumed like the drink of a drunkard— like stubble that is fully dry.
public_domain_references.web: For entangled like thorns, and drunken as with their drink, they are consumed utterly like dry stubble.
public_domain_references.asv: For entangled like thorns, and drunken as with their drink, they are consumed utterly as dry stubble.
public_domain_references.kjv: For while [they be] folden together [as] thorns, and while they are drunken [as] drunkards, they shall be devoured as stubble fully dry.
public_domain_references.brenton: For [the enemy] shall be laid bare even to the foundation, and shall be devoured as twisted yew, and as stubble fully dry.

pob.text: From you has come one who plots evil against Yahweh[a], a counselor of worthlessness.

spob.text: Someone has come from you who plots evil against Yahweh—a wicked adviser.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: From you, O Nineveh, comes forth a plotter of evil against the LORD, a counselor of wickedness.
public_domain_references.web: One has gone out of you who devises evil against Yahweh, who counsels wickedness.
public_domain_references.asv: There is one gone forth out of thee, that deviseth evil against Jehovah, that counselleth wickedness.
public_domain_references.kjv: There is [one] come out of thee, that imagineth evil against the LORD, a wicked counsellor.
public_domain_references.brenton: Out of thee shall proceed a device against the Lord, counselling evil things hostile [to him].

pob.text: Thus says the LORD: Though they are whole, and likewise many, even so they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.

spob.text: This is what the LORD says: “Though they are at full strength and numerous, they will still be cut down and pass away. I have made you suffer, but I will not make you suffer again.”

public_domain_references.bsb: This is what the LORD says: “Though they are allied and numerous, yet they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, O Judah, I will afflict you no longer.
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh says: “Though they are in full strength and likewise many, even so they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
public_domain_references.asv: Thus saith Jehovah: Though they be in full strength, and likewise many, even so shall they be cut down, and he shall pass away. Though I have afflicted thee, I will afflict thee no more.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thus saith the LORD; Though [they be] quiet, and likewise many, yet thus shall they be cut down, when he shall pass through. Though I have afflicted thee, I will afflict thee no more.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thus saith the Lord who rules over many waters, Even thus shall they be sent away, and the report of thee shall not be heard any more.

pob.text: And now I will break his yoke from upon you[a], and I will tear off your bonds.

spob.text: And now I will break his yoke off you[a], and I will tear away your bonds.

public_domain_references.bsb: For I will now break their yoke from your neck and tear away your shackles.”
public_domain_references.web: Now I will break his yoke from off you, and will burst your bonds apart.”
public_domain_references.asv: And now will I break his yoke from off thee, and will burst thy bonds in sunder.
public_domain_references.kjv: For now will I break his yoke from off thee, and will burst thy bonds in sunder.
public_domain_references.brenton: And now will I break his rod from off thee, and will burst [thy] bonds.

pob.text: Yahweh has commanded concerning you: No more will your name be sown[a]. From the house of your gods I will cut off carved image and cast image. I will make your grave[c][b], for you are contemptible.

spob.text:
Yahweh has issued this command concerning you:

“Your name will no longer be sown—that is, carried on.[a] From the temple of your gods, I will cut off carved idols and cast-metal idols.[b] I will prepare your grave, because you are contemptible.”[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: The LORD has issued a command concerning you, O Nineveh: “There will be no descendants to carry on your name. I will cut off the carved image and cast idol from the house of your gods; I will prepare your grave, for you are contemptible.”
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh has commanded concerning you: “No more descendants will bear your name. Out of the house of your gods, I will cut off the engraved image and the molten image. I will make your grave, for you are vile.”
public_domain_references.asv: And Jehovah hath given commandment concerning thee, that no more of thy name be sown: out of the house of thy gods will I cut off the graven image and the molten image; I will make thy grave; for thou art vile.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the LORD hath given a commandment concerning thee, [that] no more of thy name be sown: out of the house of thy gods will I cut off the graven image and the molten image: I will make thy grave; for thou art vile.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the Lord shall give a command concerning thee; there shall no more of thy name be scattered: I will utterly destroy the graven [images] out of the house of thy god, and the molten [images]: I will make thy grave; for [they are] swift.

pob.text: Look[a], on the mountains are the feet of one who brings good news, who announces peace. Celebrate your festivals, Judah; fulfill your vows[b], for the worthless one will never again pass through you; he is completely cut off.

spob.text: Look! The feet of someone bringing good news and announcing peace are on the mountains. Judah, celebrate your festivals and carry out the vows you made. The worthless one[a] will never again pass through you. He has been completely cut off—destroyed.

public_domain_references.bsb: One who scatters advances against you, O Nineveh. Guard the fortress! Watch the road! Brace yourselves! Summon all your strength!
public_domain_references.web: He who dashes in pieces has come up against you. Keep the fortress! Watch the way! Strengthen your waist! Fortify your power mightily!
public_domain_references.asv: He that dasheth in pieces is come up against thee: keep the fortress, watch the way, make thy loins strong, fortify thy power mightily.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that dasheth in pieces is come up before thy face: keep the munition, watch the way, make [thy] loins strong, fortify [thy] power mightily.
public_domain_references.brenton: Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that brings glad tidings, and publishes peace! O Juda, keep thy feasts, pay thy vows: for they shall no more pass through thee to [thy] decay.

pob.text: A scatterer has come up against your face[a]. Guard the fortress; watch the road; strengthen your loins[c][b]; muster your strength greatly.

spob.text: A scatterer[a] has advanced directly against you. Guard the fortress[b]! Watch the road! Brace yourself for action[c]! Gather all your strength!

public_domain_references.bsb: For the LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob like the splendor of Israel, though destroyers have laid them waste and ruined the branches of their vine.
public_domain_references.web: For Yahweh restores the excellency of Jacob as the excellency of Israel, for the destroyers have destroyed them and ruined their vine branches.
public_domain_references.asv: For Jehovah restoreth the excellency of Jacob, as the excellency of Israel; for the emptiers have emptied them out, and destroyed their vine-branches.
public_domain_references.kjv: For the LORD hath turned away the excellency of Jacob, as the excellency of Israel: for the emptiers have emptied them out, and marred their vine branches.
public_domain_references.brenton: It is all over with him, he has been removed, [one] who has been delivered from affliction has come up panting into thy presence, watch the way, strengthen [thy] loins, be very valiant in [thy] strength.

pob.text: For Yahweh is restoring the majesty of Jacob like the majesty of Israel[c][b][a], though destroyers have destroyed them and ruined their vine branches.

spob.text: For Yahweh is restoring Jacob’s majesty to be like Israel’s majesty, though plunderers have stripped them bare and ruined their vine branches.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The shields of his mighty men are red; the valiant warriors are dressed in scarlet. The fittings of the chariots flash like fire on the day they are prepared, and the spears of cypress have been brandished.
public_domain_references.web: The shield of his mighty men is made red. The valiant men are in scarlet. The chariots flash with steel in the day of his preparation, and the pine spears are brandished.
public_domain_references.asv: The shield of his mighty men is made red, the valiant men are in scarlet: the chariots flash with steel in the day of his preparation, and the cypress [spears] are brandished.
public_domain_references.kjv: The shield of his mighty men is made red, the valiant men [are] in scarlet: the chariots [shall be] with flaming torches in the day of his preparation, and the fir trees shall be terribly shaken.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the Lord has turned aside the pride of Jacob, as the pride of Israel: for they have utterly rejected them, and have destroyed their branches.

pob.text: The shield of his mighty men is red[a]; the men of valor are clothed in scarlet. The chariots flash with the fire of steel on the day of his preparation[b], and the cypress spears are brandished.

spob.text: The shields of his warriors are red, and his brave soldiers wear scarlet. When he makes ready, the chariots flash with fiery steel,[a] and cypress-wood spears are brandished.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: The chariots dash through the streets; they rush around the plazas, appearing like torches, darting about like lightning.
public_domain_references.web: The chariots rage in the streets. They rush back and forth in the wide ways. Their appearance is like torches. They run like the lightnings.
public_domain_references.asv: The chariots rage in the streets; they rush to and fro in the broad ways: the appearance of them is like torches; they run like the lightnings.
public_domain_references.kjv: The chariots shall rage in the streets, they shall justle one against another in the broad ways: they shall seem like torches, they shall run like the lightnings.
public_domain_references.brenton: [They have destroyed] the arms of their power from among men, their mighty men sporting with fire: the reins of their chariots [shall be destroyed] in the day of his preparation, and the horsemen shall be thrown into confusion

pob.text: In the streets the chariots race wildly[a]; they rattle through the squares. Their appearance is like torches[c][b]; like lightning they dart about.

spob.text: The chariots race wildly[a] through the streets, clattering[b] through the squares. They look like torches and dart back and forth like lightning.

public_domain_references.bsb: He summons his nobles; they stumble as they advance. They race to its wall; the protective shield is set in place.
public_domain_references.web: He summons his picked troops. They stumble on their way. They dash to its wall, and the protective shield is put in place.
public_domain_references.asv: He remembereth his nobles: they stumble in their march; they make haste to the wall thereof, and the mantelet is prepared.
public_domain_references.kjv: He shall recount his worthies: they shall stumble in their walk; they shall make haste to the wall thereof, and the defence shall be prepared.
public_domain_references.brenton: in the ways, and the chariots shall clash together, and shall be entangled in each other in the broad ways: their appearance is as lamps of fire, and as gleaming lightnings.

pob.text: He summons his nobles; they stumble in their march. They hurry to her wall, and the siege shelter is set up.

spob.text: He calls his nobles. They stumble as they advance. They rush to her wall, and the siege shelter is set up.

public_domain_references.bsb: The river gates are thrown open and the palace collapses.
public_domain_references.web: The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace is dissolved.
public_domain_references.asv: The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace is dissolved.
public_domain_references.kjv: The gates of the rivers shall be opened, and the palace shall be dissolved.
public_domain_references.brenton: And their mighty men shall bethink themselves and flee by day; and they shall be weak as they go; and they shall hasten to her walls, and shall prepare their defences.

pob.text: The gates of the rivers are opened[b][a], and the palace melts away.

spob.text: The river gates are opened,[a] and the palace melts away.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: It is decreed that the city be exiled and carried away; her maidservants moan like doves, and beat upon their breasts.
public_domain_references.web: It is decreed: she is uncovered, she is carried away; and her servants moan as with the voice of doves, beating on their breasts.
public_domain_references.asv: And it is decreed: she is uncovered, she is carried away; and her handmaids moan as with the voice of doves, beating upon their breasts.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Huzzab shall be led away captive, she shall be brought up, and her maids shall lead [her] as with the voice of doves, tabering upon their breasts.
public_domain_references.brenton: The gates of the cities have been opened, and the palaces have fallen into ruin,

pob.text: It is fixed: she is stripped bare[a], she is carried away; and her slave girls are led off, moaning like the sound of doves[b], beating on their hearts.

spob.text: It is settled: she is stripped bare[a] and carried away. Her slave girls are led off. Their moans sound like doves, and they beat their chests in mourning.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Nineveh has been like a pool of water throughout her days, but now it is draining away. “Stop! Stop!” they cry, but no one turns back.
public_domain_references.web: But Nineveh has been from of old like a pool of water, yet they flee away. “Stop! Stop!” they cry, but no one looks back.
public_domain_references.asv: But Nineveh hath been from of old like a pool of water: yet they flee away. Stand, stand, [they cry]; but none looketh back.
public_domain_references.kjv: But Nineveh [is] of old like a pool of water: yet they shall flee away. Stand, stand, [shall they cry;] but none shall look back.
public_domain_references.brenton: and the foundation has been exposed; and she has gone up, and her maid-servants were led [away] as doves moaning in their hearts.

pob.text: Nineveh has been like a pool of water from her earliest days[a], yet they are fleeing[b]. “Stop! Stop!”—but no one turns back.

spob.text: From her earliest days, Nineveh has been like a pool of water. But now her people are fleeing. “Stop! Stop!”[a] But no one turns back.

public_domain_references.bsb: “Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold!” There is no end to the treasure, an abundance of every precious thing.
public_domain_references.web: Take the plunder of silver. Take the plunder of gold, for there is no end of treasure, an abundance of every precious thing.
public_domain_references.asv: Take ye the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold; for there is no end of the store, the glory of all goodly furniture.
public_domain_references.kjv: Take ye the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold: for [there is] none end of the store [and] glory out of all the pleasant furniture.
public_domain_references.brenton: And [as for] Nineve, her waters [shall be] as a pool of water: and they fled, and staid not, and there was none to look back.

pob.text: Plunder silver! Plunder gold! There is no end to the treasure[b][a], an abundance of every precious thing.

spob.text: Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the stored wealth[a]—precious objects of every kind in abundance.

public_domain_references.bsb: She is emptied! Yes, she is desolate and laid waste! Hearts melt, knees knock, bodies tremble, and every face grows pale!
public_domain_references.web: She is empty, void, and waste. The heart melts, the knees knock together, their bodies and faces have grown pale.
public_domain_references.asv: She is empty, and void, and waste; and the heart melteth, and the knees smite together, and anguish is in all loins, and the faces of them all are waxed pale.
public_domain_references.kjv: She is empty, and void, and waste: and the heart melteth, and the knees smite together, and much pain [is] in all loins, and the faces of them all gather blackness.
public_domain_references.brenton: They plundered the silver, they plundered the gold, and there was no end of their adorning; they were loaded [with it] upon all their pleasant vessels.

pob.text: Devastation[a], desolation, and destruction! Hearts melt, knees give way, anguish is in every waist, and all their faces grow pale.

spob.text: Devastation, desolation, destruction! Their hearts melt with fear, and their knees give way. Anguish grips every waist, and all their faces turn pale.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Where is the lions’ lair or the feeding ground of the young lions, where the lion and lioness prowled with their cubs, with nothing to frighten them away?
public_domain_references.web: Where is the den of the lions, and the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion and the lioness walked with the lion’s cubs, and no one made them afraid?
public_domain_references.asv: Where is the den of the lions, and the feeding-place of the young lions, where the lion [and] the lioness walked, the lion’s whelp, and none made them afraid?
public_domain_references.kjv: Where [is] the dwelling of the lions, and the feedingplace of the young lions, where the lion, [even] the old lion, walked, [and] the lion’s whelp, and none made [them] afraid?
public_domain_references.brenton: [There is] thrusting forth, and shaking, and tumult, and heart-breaking, and loosing of knees, and pangs on all loins; and the faces of all [are] as the blackening of a pot.

pob.text: Where is the lions’ den[a], the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion and lioness walked, where the lion’s cub was[b], with none to make them afraid?

spob.text: Where is the lions’ den, the place where the young lions fed? The lion and lioness[a] walked there. Their cub was there too, and no one made them afraid.

public_domain_references.bsb: The lion mauled enough for its cubs and strangled prey for the lioness. It filled its dens with the kill, and its lairs with mauled prey.
public_domain_references.web: The lion tore in pieces enough for his cubs, and strangled prey for his lionesses, and filled his caves with the kill and his dens with prey.
public_domain_references.asv: The lion did tear in pieces enough for his whelps, and strangled for his lionesses, and filled his caves with prey, and his dens with ravin.
public_domain_references.kjv: The lion did tear in pieces enough for his whelps, and strangled for his lionesses, and filled his holes with prey, and his dens with ravin.
public_domain_references.brenton: Where is the dwelling-place of the lions, and the pasture that belonged to the whelps? where did the lion go, that the lion's whelp should enter in there, and there was none to scare [him] away?

pob.text: The lion tore enough for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses[b][a]; he filled his dens with prey and his lairs with torn flesh.

spob.text: The lion tore apart enough prey for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses. He filled his dens with prey and his lairs with torn flesh.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: “Behold, I am against you,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will send your chariots up in smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voices of your messengers will no longer be heard.”
public_domain_references.web: “Behold, I am against you,” says Yahweh of Armies, “and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions; and I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will no longer be heard.”
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, I am against thee, saith Jehovah of hosts, and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword shall devour thy young lions; and I will cut off thy prey from the earth, and the voice of thy messengers shall no more be heard.
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, I [am] against thee, saith the LORD of hosts, and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword shall devour thy young lions: and I will cut off thy prey from the earth, and the voice of thy messengers shall no more be heard.
public_domain_references.brenton: The lion seized enough prey for his whelps, and strangled for his [young] lions, and filled his lair with prey, and his dwelling-place with spoil.

pob.text: Woe to the city of bloodshed[a], all of it full of lies, full of plunder[d][c][b]; prey never departs.

spob.text: Woe to the city full of bloodshed! The whole city is full of lies and plunder. It never stops taking prey.

public_domain_references.bsb: Woe to the city of blood, full of lies, full of plunder, never without prey.
public_domain_references.web: Woe to the bloody city! It is all full of lies and robbery—no end to the prey.
public_domain_references.asv: Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and rapine; the prey departeth not.
public_domain_references.kjv: Woe to the bloody city! it [is] all full of lies [and] robbery; the prey departeth not;
public_domain_references.brenton: O city of blood, wholly false, full of unrighteousness; the prey shall not be handled.

pob.text: The crack of the whip[a], and the rumble of the wheel[b], with galloping horse and bounding chariot!

spob.text: The whip cracks! The wheel rumbles! The horse gallops, and the chariot bounds along!

public_domain_references.bsb: The crack of the whip, the rumble of the wheel, galloping horse and bounding chariot!
public_domain_references.web: The noise of the whip, the noise of the rattling of wheels, prancing horses, and bounding chariots,
public_domain_references.asv: The noise of the whip, and the noise of the rattling of wheels, and prancing horses, and bounding chariots,
public_domain_references.kjv: The noise of a whip, and the noise of the rattling of the wheels, and of the pransing horses, and of the jumping chariots.
public_domain_references.brenton: The noise of whips, and the noise of the rumbling of wheels, and of the pursuing horse, and of the bounding chariot,

pob.text: Horsemen charging[a], and the flashing sword and the gleaming spear, and a multitude of slain, and heaps of corpses[c][b]; and there is no end to the bodies— they stumble over the bodies.

spob.text: Horsemen charge. Swords flash, and spears gleam.[a] Many are slain, and corpses lie in heaps. There is no end to the bodies—they stumble over them.

public_domain_references.bsb: Charging horseman, flashing sword, shining spear; heaps of slain, mounds of corpses, dead bodies without end— they stumble over their dead—
public_domain_references.web: the horseman charging, and the flashing sword, the glittering spear, and a multitude of slain, and a great heap of corpses, and there is no end of the bodies. They stumble on their bodies
public_domain_references.asv: the horseman mounting, and the flashing sword, and the glittering spear, and a multitude of slain, and a great heap of corpses, and there is no end of the bodies; they stumble upon their bodies;—
public_domain_references.kjv: The horseman lifteth up both the bright sword and the glittering spear: and [there is] a multitude of slain, and a great number of carcases; and [there is] none end of [their] corpses; they stumble upon their corpses:
public_domain_references.brenton: and of the mounting rider, and of the glittering sword, and of the gleaming arms, and of a multitude of slain, and of heavy falling: and there was no end to her nations, but they shall be weak in their bodies

pob.text: because of the many prostitutions of the prostitute[a], charming in grace, mistress of sorceries[b], who sells nations by her prostitutions and clans by her sorceries.

spob.text: This is because of the prostitute’s many acts of prostitution. She is alluring and skilled in sorcery. She sells nations by means of her prostitution and clans by means of her sorcery.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: because of the many harlotries of the harlot, the seductive mistress of sorcery, who betrays nations by her prostitution and clans by her witchcraft.
public_domain_references.web: because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations through her prostitution, and families through her witchcraft.
public_domain_references.asv: because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the well-favored harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts.
public_domain_references.kjv: Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts.
public_domain_references.brenton: because of the abundance of fornication: [she is] a fair harlot, and well-favoured, skilled in sorcery, that sells the nations by her fornication, and peoples by her sorceries.

pob.text: Behold[a], I am against you, declares Yahweh of hosts, and I will uncover your skirts over your face, and I will show the nations your nakedness and the kingdoms your shame.

spob.text: “Look! I am against you,” declares Yahweh of hosts. “I will pull your skirts up over your face[a]. I will expose your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms.”

public_domain_references.bsb: “Behold, I am against you,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms.
public_domain_references.web: “Behold, I am against you,” says Yahweh of Armies, “and I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show the nations your nakedness, and the kingdoms your shame.
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, I am against thee, saith Jehovah of hosts, and I will uncover thy skirts upon thy face; and I will show the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame.
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, I [am] against thee, saith the LORD of hosts; and I will discover thy skirts upon thy face, and I will shew the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame.
public_domain_references.brenton: Behold, I am against thee, saith the Lord God Almighty, and I will uncover thy skirts in thy presence, and I will shew the nations thy shame, and the kingdoms thy disgrace.

pob.text: And I will throw filth upon you[a], and treat you with contempt[b], and make you a spectacle.

spob.text: I will throw disgusting refuse on you.[a] I will disgrace you and put you on public display.

public_domain_references.bsb: I will pelt you with filth and treat you with contempt; I will make a spectacle of you.
public_domain_references.web: I will throw abominable filth on you and make you vile, and will make you a spectacle.
public_domain_references.asv: And I will cast abominable filth upon thee, and make thee vile, and will set thee as a gazing-stock.
public_domain_references.kjv: And I will cast abominable filth upon thee, and make thee vile, and will set thee as a gazingstock.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I will cast abominable filth upon thee according to thine unclean ways, and will make thee a public example.

pob.text: And it will happen that all who see you will shrink from you and say, ‘Nineveh is devastated; who will grieve for her? Where can I seek comforters for you?’

spob.text: Everyone who sees you will flee from you and say, “Nineveh has been devastated! Who will grieve for her? Where can I find anyone to comfort you?”

public_domain_references.bsb: Then all who see you will recoil from you and say, ‘Nineveh is devastated; who will grieve for her?’ Where can I find comforters for you?”
public_domain_references.web: It will happen that all those who look at you will flee from you, and say, ‘Nineveh is laid waste! Who will mourn for her?’ Where will I seek comforters for you?”
public_domain_references.asv: And it shall come to pass, that all they that look upon thee shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her? whence shall I seek comforters for thee?
public_domain_references.kjv: And it shall come to pass, [that] all they that look upon thee shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her? whence shall I seek comforters for thee?
public_domain_references.brenton: And it shall be [that] every one that sees thee shall go down from thee, and shall say, Wretched Nineve! who shall lament for her? whence shall I seek comfort for her?

pob.text: Are you better than No-amon, who sat among the Nile channels, with waters all around her, whose rampart was the sea, whose wall was from the sea?

spob.text: Are you any better than No-amon? She sat among the channels of the Nile, with water all around her. The sea was her outer defense, and her wall came from the sea.

public_domain_references.bsb: Are you better than Thebes, stationed by the Nile with water around her, whose rampart was the sea, whose wall was the water?
public_domain_references.web: Are you better than No-Amon, who was situated among the rivers, who had the waters around her, whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was of the sea?
public_domain_references.asv: Art thou better than No-amon, that was situate among the rivers, that had the waters round about her; whose rampart was the sea, [and] her wall was of the sea?
public_domain_references.kjv: Art thou better than populous No, that was situate among the rivers, [that had] the waters round about it, whose rampart [was] the sea, [and] her wall [was] from the sea?
public_domain_references.brenton: Prepare thee a portion, tune the chord, prepare a portion for Ammon: she that dwells among the rivers, water is round about her, whose dominion is the sea, and whose walls are water.

pob.text: Cush was her strength[a], and Egypt without end[d][c][b]; Put and the Libyans were among your helpers.

spob.text: Cush was her source of strength, and Egypt’s support had no limit. Put and the Libyans were among your helpers.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength; Put and Libya were her allies.
public_domain_references.web: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength. Put and Libya were her helpers.
public_domain_references.asv: Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, and it was infinite; Put and Lubim were thy helpers.
public_domain_references.kjv: Ethiopia and Egypt [were] her strength, and [it was] infinite; Put and Lubim were thy helpers.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Ethiopia is her strength, and Egypt; and there was no limit of the flight [of her enemies]; and the Libyans became her helpers.

pob.text: Yet she too went into exile[a], into captivity; her children too were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her honored men[d][c][b], and all her great men were bound in chains.

spob.text: Yet she too was taken away into exile and captivity. Her young children too were dashed to pieces at every street entrance.[a] Her captors divided her honored men among themselves by casting lots, and all her prominent men were bound in chains.

public_domain_references.bsb: Yet she became an exile; she went into captivity. Her infants were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her dignitaries, and all her nobles were bound in chains.
public_domain_references.web: Yet was she carried away. She went into captivity. Her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of all the streets, and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
public_domain_references.asv: Yet was she carried away, she went into captivity; her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of all the streets; and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
public_domain_references.kjv: Yet [was] she carried away, she went into captivity: her young children also were dashed in pieces at the top of all the streets: and they cast lots for her honourable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
public_domain_references.brenton: Yet she shall go as a prisoner into captivity, and they shall dash her infants against the ground at the top of all her ways: and they shall cast lots upon all her glorious [possessions], and all her nobles shall be bound in chains.

pob.text: You too will become drunk[a]; you will be hidden[b]. You too will seek a refuge from the enemy.

spob.text: You too will become drunk, reeling under judgment. You will be hidden from sight. You too will look for a safe place[a] away from the enemy.

public_domain_references.bsb: You too will become drunk; you will go into hiding and seek refuge from the enemy.
public_domain_references.web: You also will be drunken. You will be hidden. You also will seek a stronghold because of the enemy.
public_domain_references.asv: Thou also shalt be drunken; thou shalt be hid; thou also shalt seek a stronghold because of the enemy.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thou also shalt be drunken: thou shalt be hid, thou also shalt seek strength because of the enemy.
public_domain_references.brenton: And thou shalt be drunken, and shalt be overlooked; and thou shalt seek for thyself strength because of [thine] enemies.

pob.text: All your fortresses are fig trees with first-ripe figs; if they are shaken[a], they fall into the mouth of the eater.

spob.text: All your fortresses are like fig trees[a] bearing first-ripe figs. If shaken, the figs fall into the eater’s mouth.

public_domain_references.bsb: All your fortresses are fig trees with the first ripe figs; when shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater!
public_domain_references.web: All your fortresses will be like fig trees with the first-ripe figs. If they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
public_domain_references.asv: All thy fortresses shall be [like] fig-trees with the first-ripe figs: if they be shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
public_domain_references.kjv: All thy strong holds [shall be like] fig trees with the firstripe figs: if they be shaken, they shall even fall into the mouth of the eater.
public_domain_references.brenton: All thy strong-holds are as fig-trees having watchers: if they be shaken, they shall fall into the mouth of the eater.

pob.text: Look[a], your troops are women in your midst; the gates of your land stand wide open to your enemies[c][b]; fire has consumed your bars.

spob.text: Look! Your troops[a] are women among you. The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies. Fire has burned up your gate-bars.

public_domain_references.bsb: Look at your troops— they are like your women! The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire consumes their bars.
public_domain_references.web: Behold, your troops among you are women. The gates of your land are set wide open to your enemies. The fire has devoured your bars.
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, thy people in the midst of thee are women; the gates of thy land are set wide open unto thine enemies: the fire hath devoured thy bars.
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, thy people in the midst of thee [are] women: the gates of thy land shall be set wide open unto thine enemies: the fire shall devour thy bars.
public_domain_references.brenton: Behold, thy people within thee are as women: the gates of thy land shall surely be opened to thine enemies: the fire shall devour thy bars.

pob.text: Draw water for yourself for the siege; strengthen your fortresses[a]. Go into the clay and tread the mortar; take hold of the brick mold.

spob.text: Draw the water you will need during the siege. Make your fortresses stronger. Step into the clay and tread the mortar with your feet. Take hold of the brick mold.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Draw your water for the siege; strengthen your fortresses. Work the clay and tread the mortar; repair the brick kiln!
public_domain_references.web: Draw water for the siege. Strengthen your fortresses. Go into the clay, and tread the mortar. Make the brick kiln strong.
public_domain_references.asv: Draw thee water for the siege; strengthen thy fortresses; go into the clay, and tread the mortar; make strong the brickkiln.
public_domain_references.kjv: Draw thee waters for the siege, fortify thy strong holds: go into clay, and tread the morter, make strong the brickkiln.
public_domain_references.brenton: Draw thee water for a siege, and well secure thy strong-holds: enter into the clay, and be thou trodden in the chaff, make [the fortifications] stronger than brick.

pob.text: There the fire will devour you; the sword will cut you off; it will devour you like the locust[a]. Multiply yourself like the locust; multiply yourself like the swarming locust.

spob.text: There, fire will devour you, and the sword will cut you off. It will devour you as a locust devours. Multiply your numbers like locusts[a]; multiply your numbers like a swarm of locusts.

public_domain_references.bsb: There the fire will devour you; the sword will cut you down and consume you like a young locust. Make yourself many like the young locust; make yourself many like the swarming locust!
public_domain_references.web: There the fire will devour you. The sword will cut you off. It will devour you like the grasshopper. Multiply like grasshoppers. Multiply like the locust.
public_domain_references.asv: There shall the fire devour thee; the sword shall cut thee off; it shall devour thee like the canker-worm: make thyself many as the canker-worm; make thyself many as the locust.
public_domain_references.kjv: There shall the fire devour thee; the sword shall cut thee off, it shall eat thee up like the cankerworm: make thyself many as the cankerworm, make thyself many as the locusts.
public_domain_references.brenton: There the fire shall devour thee; the sword shall utterly destroy thee, it shall devour thee as the locust, and thou shalt be pressed down as a palmerworm.

pob.text: You multiplied your merchants more than the stars of the heavens[b][a]; the locust strips bare and flies away.

spob.text: You made your merchants more numerous than the stars in the sky. The locust[a] strips the land bare, then flies away.

public_domain_references.bsb: You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of the sky. The young locust strips the land and flies away.
public_domain_references.web: You have increased your merchants more than the stars of the skies. The grasshopper strips and flees away.
public_domain_references.asv: Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the canker-worm ravageth, and fleeth away.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the cankerworm spoileth, and flieth away.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thou hast multiplied thy merchandise beyond the stars of heaven: the palmerworm has attacked [it], and has flown away.

pob.text: Your guards are like locusts[a], and your scribes like swarms of locusts, settling on the walls on a cold day. The sun rises, and they fly away[d][c][b]; no one knows where they are.

spob.text: Your guards[a] are like locusts, and your scribes[b] are like swarms of locusts resting on the walls on a cold day. When the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where they have gone.

public_domain_references.bsb: Your guards are like the swarming locust, and your scribes like clouds of locusts that settle on the walls on a cold day. When the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where.
public_domain_references.web: Your guards are like the locusts, and your officials like the swarms of locusts, which settle on the walls on a cold day, but when the sun appears, they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.
public_domain_references.asv: Thy princes are as the locusts, and thy marshals as the swarms of grasshoppers, which encamp in the hedges in the cold day, but when the sun ariseth they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thy crowned [are] as the locusts, and thy captains as the great grasshoppers, which camp in the hedges in the cold day, [but] when the sun ariseth they flee away, and their place is not known where they [are].
public_domain_references.brenton: Thy mixed [multitude] has suddenly departed as the grasshopper, as the locust perched on a hedge in a frosty day; the sun arises, and it flies off, and knows not its place: woe to them!

pob.text: Your shepherds slumber[a], O king of Assyria; your nobles lie down. Your people are scattered on the mountains[d][c][b], and there is no one to gather them.

spob.text: King of Assyria, your shepherds—your leaders—are asleep. Your nobles lie down, inactive.[a] Your people are scattered across the mountains,[b] and no one is there to gather them.

public_domain_references.bsb: O king of Assyria, your shepherds slumber; your officers sleep. Your people are scattered on the mountains with no one to gather them.
public_domain_references.web: Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria. Your nobles lie down. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
public_domain_references.asv: Thy shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria; thy nobles are at rest; thy people are scattered upon the mountains, and there is none to gather them.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thy shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria: thy nobles shall dwell [in the dust:] thy people is scattered upon the mountains, and no man gathereth [them].
public_domain_references.brenton: Thy shepherds have slumbered, the Assyrian king has laid low thy mighty men: thy people departed to the mountains, and there was none to receive [them].

pob.text: There is no healing for your fracture[a]; your wound is grievous. All who hear the report about you clap their hands over you[b], for over whom has your evil not continually passed?

spob.text: Your brokenness cannot be healed; your wound is severe. Everyone who hears the news about you claps at your downfall. For who has not had your evil sweep over them again and again?

public_domain_references.bsb: There is no healing for your injury; your wound is severe. All who hear the news of you applaud your downfall, for who has not experienced your constant cruelty?
public_domain_references.web: There is no healing your wound, for your injury is fatal. All who hear the report of you clap their hands over you, for who hasn’t felt your endless cruelty?
public_domain_references.asv: There is no assuaging of thy hurt; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the report of thee clap their hands over thee; for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?
public_domain_references.kjv: [There is] no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the bruit of thee shall clap the hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?
public_domain_references.brenton: There is no healing for thy bruise; thy wound has rankled: all that hear the report of thee shall clap their hands against thee; for upon whom has not thy wickedness passed continually?
